html:
Baseball reached the Dominican Republic in the late 1800s, brought by Cubans fleeing the wars on their island, and became the national sport.

Sugar mill towns such as San Pedro de Macoris formed teams, and the game spread during the US occupation. Since the 1950s Dominican players have gone north to the major leagues, and US clubs run training academies on the island.

The Dominican Republic sends more players to Major League Baseball than any country outside the United States, among them stars such as Juan Marichal, Pedro Martinez and David Ortiz. For many poor boys the game is a hope of escape, and its stars are heroes at home. The Dominican team won the World Baseball Classic in 2013.
sum: Baseball reached the Dominican Republic in the late 1800s, brought by Cubans fleeing the wars on their island, and became the national sport.
